limitations_and_boundaries: AdaEdge suffers from wrong graph adjustment operations when the ratio of incorrect operations is too large, which can bring serious interference and little or no improvement.
MADReg can hardly improve performance when over-smoothing is not severe (small number of GNN layers).
The study focuses on node classification tasks; applicability to other graph-based tasks is not explored.
The analysis is limited to the 10 GNN models and 7 datasets used; generalizability to other architectures or domains is not guaranteed.

research_questions.statement: What is the key factor leading to the over-smoothing problem in GNNs, and how can it be measured and alleviated?

provenance.text_excerpt: We observe that the MAD values of various GNNs become smaller as the number of GNN layers increases, which supports the argument that smoothing is the essential nature of GNNs.

claims.statement: Smoothing is the essential nature of GNNs.

provenance.text_excerpt: Experimental results show that the AdaEdge method can effectively improve the model performance in most cases, which proves that optimizing the graph topology is quite helpful for improving model performance.

claims.statement: AdaEdge improves model performance in most cases across 7 datasets.

provenance.text_excerpt: Above all, both AdaEdge and MADReg are effective for improving GNNs performance, and AdaEdge generalizes better when the over-smoothing issue is not severe.

claims.statement: AdaEdge generalizes better than MADReg when over-smoothing is not severe.

provenance.text_excerpt: And we can find that the two proposed methods can effectively relieve the over-smoothing issue and improve model performance in most cases.

claims.statement: MADReg and AdaEdge effectively relieve over-smoothing and improve model performance in high-order layers.

provenance.text_excerpt: To prove our assumption, we optimize the graph topology by removing inter-class edges and adding intra-class edges based on the gold labels, which proves very effective in relieving over-smoothing and improving model performance.

claims.statement: Optimizing graph topology based on gold labels effectively relieves over-smoothing and improves model performance.

provenance.text_excerpt: Further experiments show that both the model performance and the MADGap value rise as the information-to-noise ratio increases, which verifies our assumption that the information-to-noise ratio affects the smoothness of graph representation to a great extent.

claims.statement: The information-to-noise ratio affects the smoothness of graph representation.

experiments_or_tasks: Analyze the effect of information-to-noise ratio on smoothness and over-smoothness.
Apply AdaEdge (adaptive edge optimization) to iteratively adjust graph topology based on predictions.
Apply MADReg (MADGap-based regularizer) to training objective.
Evaluate AdaEdge on all 7 datasets with various GNN models.
Evaluate effect on over-smoothing and model performance.
Evaluate on 10 GNN models with 4 layers on CORA, CiteSeer, PubMed.
Measure over-smoothness using MADGap and correlate with model performance.
Measure smoothness of node representations using MAD on multiple GNN models and layers.
Optimize graph topology by removing inter-class edges and adding intra-class edges based on gold labels.
